links.targetTitle: Ecosystem Accords make Agent-to-Agent agreements a first-cla
Osero's relationship with Sky rests on a bilateral Ecosystem

title: Ecosystem Accords bind an Agent to Sky by mutual agreement recorded in both Artifacts
content:
A.6.1.1.3.3.3 states that "Keel has formally agreed to the Ecosystem Accords herein," and A.6.1.1.3.3.3.1 records that "Keel engaged in terms of agreement with Sky in Ecosystem Accord 3," pointing to A.2.8.2.3 - Ecosystem Accord 3: Sky And Keel.

The structure is bilateral in a way most of the Atlas is not. Elsewhere, Sky sets rules and Agent Artifacts implement them; here the Accord is described as "terms of agreement" that Keel "engaged in" and "formally agreed to" — the language of contract between parties, not of mandate from a superior. The Accord itself is titled with both names.

The placement is equally deliberate. The terms live in Sky's branch (A.2.8), while the Agent's Artifact holds only the record of assent and a pointer. That means there is exactly one authoritative text for the Accord, and no possibility of the Agent's copy drifting from Sky's copy — a single-source-of-truth discipline applied to inter-party agreements.

The cost is that reading Keel's Artifact alone tells you Keel is bound by Accord 3 but not what Accord 3 requires. Assent and content are separated, so an auditor must traverse to Sky's tree to learn the obligations, and Keel's own document cannot be relied on as a complete statement of its commitments.
description: Keel "formally agreed" to Ecosystem Accord 3, whose terms live in Sky's own tree at A.2.8.2.3 — the Agent Artifact records assent by reference rather than restating the terms.
